335.impactEvidence: Verified by direct WCAG contrast computation: --text-dim (#758189) vs --btn (#14181b) = 4.47:1 and --bad (#c56164) vs --btn (#14181b) = 4.48:1, both just under the 4.5:1 AA text threshold (web/src/styles/tokens.css:20,33,43). --tick-queued (#2a2f34) vs --tick-off (#1d2125) = 1.20:1, well under the 3:1 non-text threshold required by WCAG 1.4.11 (web/src/styles/tokens.css:45-46), and these two tokens are the fill/track pair for every progress bar rendered by web/src/components/tui/Ticks.tsx:10 and web/src/components/tui/Ticks.module.css:9, wired into Overview, Jobs, JobDetail and UploadsPanel. All of this is a visual/legibility degradation only — text stays readable via other channels (icons/labels/position), no functionality breaks, no data loss, no outage risk. That keeps it at cosmetic rather than degraded, per the rubric's "worst outcome the defect can produce": worst case is a queued-vs-off tick barely distinguishable in a progress bar, not a broken feature.
